relationships.subject: Bradykinin
relationships.evidence_quote: acute (2-3 min) application of 100nM BK led to spontaneous activity or depolarization in 75% of neurons recorded

relationships.subject: Bradykinin
relationships.evidence_quote: Among repetitive-spiking neurons, prolonged exposure to BK led to an overall reduction in excitability

relationships.subject: B2 receptor
relationships.evidence_quote: A majority (72.4%) of BDKRB2-expressing neurons also expressed SCN10A, indicating that BDKRB2-expressing cells are predominantly nociceptors

relationships.subject: B2 receptor
relationships.evidence_quote: we also observed that BDKRB2 co-localized with FABP7, a marker of satellite glial cells

key_findings: B2 receptor mRNA is expressed in ~48-61% of human DRG neurons, enriched in SCN10A+ nociceptors, and B1 only in <10%.
Acute bradykinin increases human DRG neuron excitability while prolonged exposure reduces it in repetitive-spiking neurons.
